newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seas delay survey of disabled Australia rig.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seas delay survey of disabled Australia rig.

text.p: Choppy seas on Monday prevented divers inspecting an 8,500 tonne drilling rig disabled during installation at the weekend offshore South Australia, a spokesman for explorer Canyon (Australia) Pty Ltd said.
Chris Rann told Reuters the Maersk Victory sustained further damage early on Monday when the top portion of one of its legs broke off and came to rest on the rig's helipad.

Asked whether there was any risk the structure could sink, Rann said officials could not determine either the stability of the rig nor its repair options until the underwater inspection could be carried out.
Local sources said a salvage operation was more likely than on-the-spot repair, with the rig expected to be transported by owner/operator Maersk Drilling (Australia) Ltd for repair at an Asian port.

About 35 workers were evacuated on Saturday when one of the rig's legs struck unstable ground while being positioned at the Enchilada No. 1 drill site for a A$15 million petroleum exploration program by Canyon in St Vincent's Gulf.
Canyon is 100 percent owned by private Texan based oil and gas explorer and producer Wagner and Brown Ltd.
Rann said eight specialist divers were on standby to begin their inspection as soon as conditions permitted.
